    56	/-- An expanded point effect is self-adjoint. -/
    57	theorem pointMeasExp_effect_conjTranspose (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
    58	    (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind) (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)
    59	    (a : PauliScalar P) :
    60	    ((S.pointMeasExp side W u).effect a)ᴴ = (S.pointMeasExp side W u).effect a :=
    61	  (S.pointMeasExp_isProjective side W u a).isSelfAdjoint.isHermitian.eq
    62	
    63	/-- An expanded point effect is idempotent. -/
    64	theorem pointMeasExp_effect_mul_self (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
    65	    (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind) (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)
    66	    (a : PauliScalar P) :
    67	    (S.pointMeasExp side W u).effect a * (S.pointMeasExp side W u).effect a =
    68	      (S.pointMeasExp side W u).effect a :=
    69	  (S.pointMeasExp_isProjective side W u a).isIdempotentElem.eq
    70	
    71	/-- The sandwich `M^Z_b M^X_a M^Z_b` is `(M^X_a M^Z_b)ᴴ (M^X_a M^Z_b)`. -/
    72	theorem sandwich_eq_conjTranspose_mul_self (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
    73	    (side : PlayerSide) (x z : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) (a b : PauliScalar P) :
    74	    (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect b * (S.pointMeasExp side .X x).effect a *
    75	        (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect b =
    76	      ((S.pointMeasExp side .X x).effect a * (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect b)ᴴ *
    77	        ((S.pointMeasExp side .X x).effect a * (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect b) := by
    78	  rw [Matrix.conjTranspose_mul, pointMeasExp_effect_conjTranspose,
    79	    pointMeasExp_effect_conjTranspose, Matrix.mul_assoc _ _
    80	      ((S.pointMeasExp side .X x).effect a * (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect b),
    81	    ← Matrix.mul_assoc ((S.pointMeasExp side .X x).effect a)
    82	      ((S.pointMeasExp side .X x).effect a), pointMeasExp_effect_mul_self,
    83	    ← Matrix.mul_assoc]
    84	
    85	/-- The sandwich effects resolve the identity. -/
    86	theorem sum_sandwich_eq_one (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide)
    87	    (x z : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) :
    88	    ∑ ab : PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P,
    89	        (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect ab.2 *
    90	          (S.pointMeasExp side .X x).effect ab.1 *
    91	          (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect ab.2 = 1 := by
    92	  rw [Fintype.sum_prod_type_right]
    93	  calc ∑ b : PauliScalar P, ∑ a : PauliScalar P,
    94	        (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect b * (S.pointMeasExp side .X x).effect a *
    95	          (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect b
    96	      = ∑ b : PauliScalar P, (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect b *
    97	          (∑ a : PauliScalar P, (S.pointMeasExp side .X x).effect a) *
    98	          (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect b := by
    99	        refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun b _ => ?_
   100	        rw [Finset.mul_sum, Finset.sum_mul]
   101	    _ = 1 := by
   102	        simp_rw [(S.pointMeasExp side .X x).sum_eq_one, mul_one,
   103	          pointMeasExp_effect_mul_self]
   104	        exact (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).sum_eq_one
   105	
   106	/-- The sandwich POVM `R^{x,z}_{a,b} = M^Z_b M^X_a M^Z_b` of the two expanded
   107	point measurements, with outcomes in `F_q × F_q`.  This is the POVM of the
   108	first step of the proof of `lem:qld-4-10`, paper
   109	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:731-736`,
   110	formed directly with field-valued outcomes rather than from the binary
   111	refinements; see `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_linearity-theorem-quotation.tex`. -/
   112	def sandwichPoint (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide)
   113	    (x z : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) :
   114	    Measurement (PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P) (S.ExpandedLocalSpace side) :=
   115	  Measurement.ofSumEqOne
   116	    (fun ab => (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect ab.2 *
   117	      (S.pointMeasExp side .X x).effect ab.1 *
   118	      (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect ab.2)
   119	    (fun ab => by
   120	      rw [sandwich_eq_conjTranspose_mul_self]
   121	      exact Matrix.nonneg_iff_posSemidef.mpr
   122	        (Matrix.posSemidef_conjTranspose_mul_self _))
   123	    (sum_sandwich_eq_one S side x z)
   124	
   125	/-- The effects of the sandwich POVM. -/
   126	@[simp] theorem sandwichPoint_effect (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
   127	    (side : PlayerSide) (x z : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)
   128	    (ab : PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P) :
   129	    (S.sandwichPoint side x z).effect ab =
   130	      (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect ab.2 *
   131	        (S.pointMeasExp side .X x).effect ab.1 *
   132	        (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect ab.2 := rfl
   133	
   134	/-- The sandwich differs from the ordered product `M^Z_b M^X_a` by
   135	`M^Z_b` times the commutator.  This is the algebra behind display
   136	`eq:qld-r-2`, paper
   137	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:737-742`. -/
   138	theorem sandwichPoint_effect_sub_ordered (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
   139	    (side : PlayerSide) (x z : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)
   140	    (ab : PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P) :
   141	    (S.sandwichPoint side x z).effect ab -
   142	        (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect ab.2 *
   143	          (S.pointMeasExp side .X x).effect ab.1 =
   144	      (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect ab.2 *
   145	        ((S.pointMeasExp side .X x).effect ab.1 *
   146	            (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect ab.2 -
   147	          (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect ab.2 *
   148	            (S.pointMeasExp side .X x).effect ab.1) := by
   149	  rw [sandwichPoint_effect, mul_sub, ← Matrix.mul_assoc, ← Matrix.mul_assoc,
   150	    pointMeasExp_effect_mul_self]
   151	
   152	/-- The sandwich POVM is close to the ordered product `M^Z_b M^X_a` on every
   153	register placement, on average over the point pair, with the error of
   154	`lem:qld-comm-cons`.  This is display `eq:qld-r-2` of the proof of
   155	`lem:qld-4-10`, paper
   156	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:737-742`, with
   157	field-valued outcomes. -/
   158	theorem sandwichPoint_ordered_dist_le :
   159	    ∃ C : ℝ, 1 ≤ C ∧
   160	      ∀ (P : AdmissibleParams) (ε : ℝ) (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
   161	        (p : Placement),
   162	        opFamilyDistSq (uniformDistribution (PointPair P))
   163	          (fun xz (ab : PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P) => S.place p
   164	            ((S.sandwichPoint p.side xz.1 xz.2).effect ab))
   165	          (fun xz ab => S.place p
   166	            ((S.pointMeasExp p.side .Z xz.2).effect ab.2 *
   167	              (S.pointMeasExp p.side .X xz.1).effect ab.1))
   168	          S.psiHat ≤ C * Real.sqrt ε := by
   169	  obtain ⟨C, hC, h⟩ := expPoint_comm
   170	  refine ⟨C, hC, fun P ε S p => le_trans ?_ (h P ε S p)⟩
   171	  unfold opFamilyDistSq
   172	  refine avgOver_mono _ _ _ fun xz => Finset.sum_le_sum fun ab _ => ?_
   173	  rw [← place_sub, sandwichPoint_effect_sub_ordered, place_mul,
   174	    applyOperatorToState_mul', ← place_sub]
   175	  exact pow_le_pow_left₀ (norm_nonneg _)
   176	    (MagicSquareRigidity.norm_applyOperatorToState_le
   177	      (S.place_conjTranspose_mul_self_le_one p
   178	        (S.pointMeasExp_isProjective p.side .Z xz.2 ab.2)) _) 2

   180	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: the placed effects of an expanded point
   181	measurement are square-summable to the identity. -/
   182	theorem sum_place_pointMeasExp_conjTranspose_mul_self (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
   183	    (p : Placement) (W : PauliKind) (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) :
   184	    ∑ a : PauliScalar P, (S.place p ((S.pointMeasExp p.side W u).effect a))ᴴ *
   185	        S.place p ((S.pointMeasExp p.side W u).effect a) ≤ 1 := by
   186	  refine le_of_eq ?_
   187	  calc ∑ a : PauliScalar P, (S.place p ((S.pointMeasExp p.side W u).effect a))ᴴ *
   188	        S.place p ((S.pointMeasExp p.side W u).effect a)
   189	      = ∑ a : PauliScalar P, S.place p ((S.pointMeasExp p.side W u).effect a) := by
   190	        refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => ?_
   191	        rw [← place_conjTranspose, ← place_mul, pointMeasExp_effect_conjTranspose,
   192	          pointMeasExp_effect_mul_self]
   193	    _ = 1 := by
   194	        rw [← place_finsetSum, (S.pointMeasExp p.side W u).sum_eq_one, place_one]
   195	
   196	/-- The ordered product `M^Z_b M^X_a` on one placement is close to the

   198	over the point pair, with the self-consistency error of `lem:qld-comm-cons`.

   203	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:851-870`. -/
   204	theorem ordered_cross_dist_le :
   205	    ∃ C : ℝ, 1 ≤ C ∧
   206	      ∀ (P : AdmissibleParams) (ε : ℝ) (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
   207	        (p₁ p₂ : Placement), p₁.IsOpposite p₂ →
   208	        opFamilyDistSq (uniformDistribution (PointPair P))
   209	          (fun xz (ab : PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P) => S.place p₁
   210	            ((S.pointMeasExp p₁.side .Z xz.2).effect ab.2 *
   211	              (S.pointMeasExp p₁.side .X xz.1).effect ab.1))

   213	            ((S.pointMeasExp p₂.side .X xz.1).effect ab.1 *
   214	              (S.pointMeasExp p₂.side .Z xz.2).effect ab.2))

   218	  intro P ε S p₁ p₂ hopp

   231	      (β := Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)

   236	    refine avgOver_mono _ _ _ fun xz => ?_

   238	        S.place p₁ ((S.pointMeasExp p₁.side .Z xz.2).effect ab.2 *
   239	            (S.pointMeasExp p₁.side .X xz.1).effect ab.1) -
   240	          S.place p₁ ((S.pointMeasExp p₁.side .Z xz.2).effect ab.2) *
   241	            S.place p₂ ((S.pointMeasExp p₂.side .X xz.1).effect ab.1) =

   257	        S.place p₁ ((S.pointMeasExp p₁.side .Z xz.2).effect ab.2) *
   258	          S.place p₂ ((S.pointMeasExp p₂.side .X xz.1).effect ab.1))
   259	      (fun xz ab => S.place p₂
   260	        ((S.pointMeasExp p₂.side .X xz.1).effect ab.1 *
   261	          (S.pointMeasExp p₂.side .Z xz.2).effect ab.2))
   262	      S.psiHat ≤ C * ε := by
   263	    refine le_trans ?_ (le_of_eq_of_le (avgOver_uniform_snd
   264	      (α := Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)
   265	      (fun z => ∑ b : PauliScalar P, ‖applyOperatorToState
   266	        (S.place p₁ ((S.pointMeasExp p₁.side .Z z).effect b) -

   268	    unfold opFamilyDistSq
   269	    refine avgOver_mono _ _ _ fun xz => ?_
   270	    have hpt : ∀ ab : PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P,
   271	        S.place p₁ ((S.pointMeasExp p₁.side .Z xz.2).effect ab.2) *
   272	            S.place p₂ ((S.pointMeasExp p₂.side .X xz.1).effect ab.1) -

   282	          ((S.pointMeasExp p₂.side .X xz.1).effect ab.1), ← mul_sub]
   283	    simp only [hpt, Fintype.sum_prod_type_right]
   284	    refine Finset.sum_le_sum fun b _ => ?_
   285	    exact DistanceCalculus.sum_norm_mul_apply_le
   286	      (fun a => S.place p₂ ((S.pointMeasExp p₂.side .X xz.1).effect a))
   287	      (S.place p₁ ((S.pointMeasExp p₁.side .Z xz.2).effect b) -
   288	        S.place p₂ ((S.pointMeasExp p₂.side .Z xz.2).effect b)) S.psiHat
   289	      (S.sum_place_pointMeasExp_conjTranspose_mul_self p₂ .X xz.1)

  obtain ⟨C₂, hC₂, h₂⟩ := expPoint_comm

        (S.place p₁ ((S.pointMeasExp p₁.side .X x).effect a) -
          S.place p₂ ((S.pointMeasExp p₂.side .X x).effect a)) S.psiHat‖ ^ 2)]

  have hK₂ := h₂ P ε S p₂

   185	private theorem avg_affine_fiber_norm_sq_le
   186	    {K ι : Type*} [Field K] [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K]
   187	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   188	    (v : K × K → EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) (hsum : ∑ p, v p = 0) :
   189	    avgOver (uniformDistribution (K × K)) (fun coefficients =>
   190	        ∑ c : K,
   191	          ‖∑ p ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun p =>
   192	            coefficients.1 * p.1 + coefficients.2 * p.2 = c), v p‖ ^ 2) ≤
   193	      ∑ p, ‖v p‖ ^ 2 := by
   194	  classical
   195	  let w : (K × K) → (K × K) → ℝ := fun p p' => (inner ℂ (v p) (v p')).re
   196	  let qinv : ℝ := (Fintype.card K : ℝ)⁻¹
   197	  have hall : (∑ p, ∑ p', w p p') = 0 := by
   198	    have h := sum_fiber_norm_sq_eq_pair_sum (fun _ : K × K => ()) v
   199	    simpa [w, hsum] using h.symm
   200	  have hdiag : (∑ p, w p p) = ∑ p, ‖v p‖ ^ 2 := by
   201	    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   202	    intro p _
   203	    exact (@norm_sq_eq_re_inner ℂ _ _ _ _ (v p)).symm
   204	  have hnonneg : 0 ≤ ∑ p, ‖v p‖ ^ 2 :=
   205	    Finset.sum_nonneg fun p _ => sq_nonneg _
   206	  have hqinv : 0 ≤ qinv := by positivity
   207	  calc
   208	    avgOver (uniformDistribution (K × K)) (fun coefficients =>
   209	        ∑ c : K,
   210	          ‖∑ p ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun p =>
   211	            coefficients.1 * p.1 + coefficients.2 * p.2 = c), v p‖ ^ 2) =
   212	        avgOver (uniformDistribution (K × K)) (fun coefficients =>
   213	          ∑ p, ∑ p', if
   214	            coefficients.1 * p.1 + coefficients.2 * p.2 =
   215	              coefficients.1 * p'.1 + coefficients.2 * p'.2 then w p p' else 0) := by
   216	            apply avgOver_congr
   217	            intro coefficients
   218	            exact sum_fiber_norm_sq_eq_pair_sum _ v
   219	    _ = ∑ p, ∑ p', avgOver (uniformDistribution (K × K)) (fun coefficients =>
   220	          if coefficients.1 * p.1 + coefficients.2 * p.2 =
   221	              coefficients.1 * p'.1 + coefficients.2 * p'.2 then w p p' else 0) := by
   222	            rw [avgOver_sum]
   223	            apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   224	            intro p _
   225	            rw [avgOver_sum]
   226	    _ = ∑ p, ∑ p', if p = p' then w p p' else qinv * w p p' := by
   227	            apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   228	            intro p _
   229	            apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   230	            intro p' _
   231	            calc
   232	              avgOver (uniformDistribution (K × K)) (fun coefficients =>
   233	                  if coefficients.1 * p.1 + coefficients.2 * p.2 =
   234	                      coefficients.1 * p'.1 + coefficients.2 * p'.2 then
   235	                    w p p' else 0) =
   236	                  avgOver (uniformDistribution (K × K)) (fun coefficients =>
   237	                    (if coefficients.1 * p.1 + coefficients.2 * p.2 =
   238	                        coefficients.1 * p'.1 + coefficients.2 * p'.2 then
   239	                      (1 : ℝ) else 0) * w p p') := by
   240	                        apply avgOver_congr
   241	                        intro coefficients
   242	                        split <;> simp_all
   243	              _ = (if p = p' then 1 else qinv) * w p p' := by
   244	                    rw [avgOver_mul_const, affine_collision_average]
   245	              _ = if p = p' then w p p' else qinv * w p p' := by
   246	                    split <;> simp_all
   247	    _ = (1 - qinv) * ∑ p, ‖v p‖ ^ 2 := by
   248	          calc
   249	            (∑ p, ∑ p', if p = p' then w p p' else qinv * w p p') =
   250	                qinv * (∑ p, ∑ p', w p p') + (1 - qinv) * ∑ p, w p p := by
   251	                  rw [Finset.mul_sum, Finset.mul_sum]
   252	                  rw [← Finset.sum_add_distrib]
   253	                  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   254	                  intro p _
   255	                  calc
   256	                    (∑ p', if p = p' then w p p' else qinv * w p p') =
   257	                        ∑ p', (qinv * w p p' +
   258	                          if p = p' then (1 - qinv) * w p p' else 0) := by
   259	                            apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   260	                            intro p' _
   261	                            by_cases h : p = p' <;> simp [h]
   262	                            ring
   263	                    _ = qinv * ∑ p', w p p' + (1 - qinv) * w p p := by
   264	                          rw [Finset.sum_add_distrib, ← Finset.mul_sum]
   265	                          congr 1
   266	                          rw [Fintype.sum_eq_single p]
   267	                          · simp
   268	                          · intro p' hp'
   269	                            simp [Ne.symm hp']
   270	            _ = (1 - qinv) * ∑ p, ‖v p‖ ^ 2 := by rw [hall, hdiag]; ring
   271	    _ ≤ ∑ p, ‖v p‖ ^ 2 := by nlinarith

   273	/-- Uniform affine scalar coarse-graining does not increase the squared
   274	state-dependent distance of complete operator families. -/
   275	theorem opFamilyDistSq_uniform_affine_postprocess_le
   276	    {X K ι : Type} [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Nonempty X]
   277	    [Field K] [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K]
   278	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   279	    (A B : X → K × K → Op ι) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι)
   280	    (hsum : ∀ x, ∑ p, A x p = ∑ p, B x p) :
   281	    opFamilyDistSq (uniformDistribution (X × (K × K)))
   282	        (fun question c =>
   283	          ∑ p ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun p =>
   284	            question.2.1 * p.1 + question.2.2 * p.2 = c), A question.1 p)
   285	        (fun question c =>
   286	          ∑ p ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun p =>
   287	            question.2.1 * p.1 + question.2.2 * p.2 = c), B question.1 p)
   288	        ψ ≤ opFamilyDistSq (uniformDistribution X) A B ψ := by
   289	  classical
   290	  unfold opFamilyDistSq
   291	  calc
   292	    avgOver (uniformDistribution (X × (K × K))) (fun question =>
   293	        ∑ c : K,
   294	          ‖applyOperatorToState
   295	            ((∑ p ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun p =>
   296	                question.2.1 * p.1 + question.2.2 * p.2 = c), A question.1 p) -
   297	              ∑ p ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun p =>
   298	                question.2.1 * p.1 + question.2.2 * p.2 = c), B question.1 p) ψ‖ ^ 2) =
   299	        avgOver (uniformDistribution X) (fun x =>
   300	          avgOver (uniformDistribution (K × K)) (fun coefficients =>
   301	            ∑ c : K,
   302	              ‖applyOperatorToState
   303	                ((∑ p ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun p =>
   304	                    coefficients.1 * p.1 + coefficients.2 * p.2 = c), A x p) -
   305	                  ∑ p ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun p =>
   306	                    coefficients.1 * p.1 + coefficients.2 * p.2 = c), B x p) ψ‖ ^ 2)) := by
   307	          simpa only using (avgOver_uniform_prod (α := X) (β := K × K)
   308	            (fun x coefficients =>
   309	              ∑ c : K,
   310	                ‖applyOperatorToState
   311	                  ((∑ p ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun p =>
   312	                      coefficients.1 * p.1 + coefficients.2 * p.2 = c), A x p) -
   313	                    ∑ p ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun p =>
   314	                      coefficients.1 * p.1 + coefficients.2 * p.2 = c), B x p) ψ‖ ^ 2))
   315	    _ ≤ avgOver (uniformDistribution X) (fun x =>
   316	        ∑ p, ‖applyOperatorToState (A x p - B x p) ψ‖ ^ 2) := by
   317	      apply avgOver_mono
   318	      intro x
   319	      let v : K × K → EuclideanSpace ℂ ι := fun p =>
   320	        applyOperatorToState (A x p - B x p) ψ
   321	      have hvsum : ∑ p, v p = 0 := by
   322	        simp only [v]
   323	        calc
   324	          (∑ p, applyOperatorToState (A x p - B x p) ψ) =
   325	              applyOperatorToState (∑ p, (A x p - B x p)) ψ :=
   326	                (MagicSquareRigidity.applyOperatorToState_sum
   327	                  (fun p => A x p - B x p) ψ).symm
   328	          _ = 0 := by
   329	            rw [Finset.sum_sub_distrib, hsum x, sub_self]
   330	            simp [applyOperatorToState]
   331	      calc
   332	        avgOver (uniformDistribution (K × K)) (fun coefficients =>
   333	            ∑ c : K,
   334	              ‖applyOperatorToState
   335	                ((∑ p ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun p =>
   336	                    coefficients.1 * p.1 + coefficients.2 * p.2 = c), A x p) -
   337	                  ∑ p ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun p =>
   338	                    coefficients.1 * p.1 + coefficients.2 * p.2 = c), B x p) ψ‖ ^ 2) =
   339	            avgOver (uniformDistribution (K × K)) (fun coefficients =>
   340	              ∑ c : K,
   341	                ‖∑ p ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun p =>
   342	                  coefficients.1 * p.1 + coefficients.2 * p.2 = c), v p‖ ^ 2) := by
   343	                  apply avgOver_congr
   344	                  intro coefficients
   345	                  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   346	                  intro c _
   347	                  congr 2
   348	                  simp only [v, applyOperatorToState, map_sub, LinearMap.sub_apply,
   349	                    map_sum, LinearMap.sum_apply, Finset.sum_sub_distrib]
   350	        _ ≤ ∑ p, ‖v p‖ ^ 2 := avg_affine_fiber_norm_sq_le v hvsum
   351	        _ = ∑ p, ‖applyOperatorToState (A x p - B x p) ψ‖ ^ 2 := rfl

/-- Register placement distributes over a filtered outcome sum. -/
private theorem place_finset_sum {P : AdmissibleParams} {ε : ℝ}
    (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (p : Placement) {α : Type*}
    (s : Finset α) (A : α → Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace p.side)) :
    S.place p (∑ a ∈ s, A a) = ∑ a ∈ s, S.place p (A a) := by
  classical
  ext i j
  cases p <;> simp [ProjectiveSetting.place, Matrix.sum_apply,
    Finset.sum_mul, Finset.mul_sum]

/-- Projectivity and the three data-processed consistency guarantees for
`CombinedPointsWitness.extendedQ`.  This is `lem:qld-4-12`, paper lines
993--1011; the `XZ` and `ZX` source products remain separate. -/
theorem extendedQ_spec {P : AdmissibleParams} {ε δ : ℝ}
    {S : ProjectiveSetting P ε} (points : CombinedPointsWitness S δ) :
    (∀ side x z alpha beta,
      Measurement.IsProjective (points.extendedQ side x z alpha beta)) ∧
    (∀ p1 p2 : Placement, p1.IsOpposite p2 ->
      opFamilyDistSq (uniformDistribution (ExtendedPointQuestion P))
        (fun question c => S.place p1
          ((points.extendedQ p1.side question.1.1 question.1.2
            question.2.1 question.2.2).effect c))
        (fun question c => S.place p2
          ((points.extendedQ p2.side question.1.1 question.1.2
            question.2.1 question.2.2).effect c))
        S.psiHat <= δ) ∧
    (∀ p1 p2 : Placement, p1.IsOpposite p2 ->
      opFamilyDistSq (uniformDistribution (ExtendedPointQuestion P))
        (fun question c => S.place p1
          ((points.extendedQ p1.side question.1.1 question.1.2
            question.2.1 question.2.2).effect c))
        (fun question c => S.place p2
          (∑ ab ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun ab : PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P =>
              question.2.1 * ab.1 + question.2.2 * ab.2 = c),
            (S.pointMeasExp p2.side .X question.1.1).effect ab.1 *
              (S.pointMeasExp p2.side .Z question.1.2).effect ab.2))
        S.psiHat <= δ) ∧
    ∀ p1 p2 : Placement, p1.IsOpposite p2 ->
      opFamilyDistSq (uniformDistribution (ExtendedPointQuestion P))
        (fun question c => S.place p1
          ((points.extendedQ p1.side question.1.1 question.1.2
            question.2.1 question.2.2).effect c))
        (fun question c => S.place p2
          (∑ ab ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun ab : PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P =>
              question.2.1 * ab.1 + question.2.2 * ab.2 = c),
            (S.pointMeasExp p2.side .Z question.1.2).effect ab.2 *
              (S.pointMeasExp p2.side .X question.1.1).effect ab.1))
        S.psiHat <= δ := by
  classical
  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro side x z alpha beta
    exact SandwichProduct.postprocess_isProjective _ (points.projective side x z) _
  · intro p1 p2 hopposite
    let A : ((Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) × (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)) →
        (PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P) → Op (SixReg P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB) :=
      fun xz ab => S.place p1 ((points.Q p1.side xz.1 xz.2).effect ab)
    let B : ((Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) × (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)) →
        (PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P) → Op (SixReg P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB) :=
      fun xz ab => S.place p2 ((points.Q p2.side xz.1 xz.2).effect ab)
    refine le_trans ?_ (points.self_consistent p1 p2 hopposite)
    have h := opFamilyDistSq_uniform_affine_postprocess_le A B S.psiHat (fun xz => ?_)
    · simpa only [A, B, CombinedPointsWitness.extendedQ,
        Measurement.postprocess_effect, place_finset_sum] using h
    · rw [sum_placed_measurement_eq_one, sum_placed_measurement_eq_one]
  · intro p1 p2 hopposite
    let A : ((Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) × (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)) →
        (PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P) → Op (SixReg P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB) :=
      fun xz ab => S.place p1 ((points.Q p1.side xz.1 xz.2).effect ab)
    let B : ((Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) × (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)) →
        (PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P) → Op (SixReg P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB) :=
      fun xz ab => S.place p2
        ((S.pointMeasExp p2.side .X xz.1).effect ab.1 *
          (S.pointMeasExp p2.side .Z xz.2).effect ab.2)
    refine le_trans ?_ (points.consistent_XZ p1 p2 hopposite)
    have h := opFamilyDistSq_uniform_affine_postprocess_le A B S.psiHat (fun xz => ?_)
    · simpa only [A, B, CombinedPointsWitness.extendedQ,
        Measurement.postprocess_effect, place_finset_sum] using h
    · rw [sum_placed_measurement_eq_one, sum_placed_measurement_products_eq_one]
  · intro p1 p2 hopposite
    let A : ((Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) × (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)) →
        (PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P) → Op (SixReg P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB) :=
      fun xz ab => S.place p1 ((points.Q p1.side xz.1 xz.2).effect ab)
    let B : ((Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) × (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)) →
        (PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P) → Op (SixReg P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB) :=
      fun xz ab => S.place p2
        ((S.pointMeasExp p2.side .Z xz.2).effect ab.2 *
          (S.pointMeasExp p2.side .X xz.1).effect ab.1)
    refine le_trans ?_ (points.consistent_ZX p1 p2 hopposite)
    have h := opFamilyDistSq_uniform_affine_postprocess_le A B S.psiHat (fun xz => ?_)
    · simpa only [A, B, CombinedPointsWitness.extendedQ,
        Measurement.postprocess_effect, place_finset_sum] using h
    · rw [sum_placed_measurement_eq_one]
      have htotal := sum_placed_measurement_products_eq_one S p2
        (S.pointMeasExp p2.side .Z xz.2) (S.pointMeasExp p2.side .X xz.1)
      rw [Fintype.sum_prod_type, Finset.sum_comm] at htotal
      simpa only [B, Fintype.sum_prod_type] using htotal.symm

end

    19	\section{At a glance}
    20	
    21	\begin{itemize}
    22	  \item \textbf{Difficulty.} Medium.  The source quotes a fiberwise consequence
    23	  of a state-dependent quantum linearity theorem, but suppresses an average,
    24	  inserts an unnecessary bound on the error, appends an identity at the origin,
    25	  and leaves implicit an ancilla assumption on the strategy.  The factor of two
    26	  lost between measurement distance and operator distance is not one of these:
    27	  it is a defect of the provider's own printed statement, treated in a separate
    28	  note.
    29	  \item \textbf{Estimated weight.} Resolved.  The corrected single-family
    30	  theorem and its two distance formulations are proved, and so is its
    31	  common-ancilla form: the ancillary space and vector of the Fourier--Naimark
    32	  argument depend only on the length of the index group.  The remaining
    33	  obligation was not the uniformity of the ancilla but the source's assumption
    34	  that the strategy carries zero-state padding.  That assumption is not part of the formal
    35	  setting, and the combined point measurements of the source's Lemma~4.10 are
    36	  therefore constructed on the original space by a route that needs no
    37	  ancilla: the sandwich of the two expanded point measurements, with outcomes
    38	  in $\F_q^2$ from the start, is approximately self-consistent by the same
    39	  calculation as in the source, and the orthonormalization lemma makes it
    40	  projective.  The only new ingredient is a Parseval identity transferring
    41	  the approximate commutation of the binary refinements to the
    42	  $\F_q$-valued measurements without loss.
    43	  \item \textbf{Mathlib/project split.} Finite Fourier orthogonality on a
    44	  finite field, inner-product expansions of squared norms, and the
    45	  submatrix/Kronecker calculus of positive semidefinite matrices are standard.
    46	  The Fourier--Naimark stability theorem, the orthonormalization lemma with
    47	  explicit constant, the expanded-state placement bookkeeping, and the
    48	  approximate commutation of the expanded point projections are project-level
    49	  results.
    50	  \item \textbf{Key mathematical inputs.} Theorem~10 of
    51	  \cite{Natarajan2017Linearity}, the operator BLR identity, Parseval's identity
    52	  for the additive characters of $\F_q$, the orthonormalization lemma of
    53	  \cite{Ji2020MIPStar} in its explicit-constant form, Jensen's inequality for
    54	  the concave function $x \mapsto x^{1/4}$, and the invariance of the expanded

    60	\section{Key theorem forms}
    61	
    62	Let $H$ be a finite-dimensional Hilbert space, let $\rho$ be an arbitrary
    63	density operator on $H$, and let $u\mapsto O^u$ be binary observables on $H$,
    64	indexed by $\F_2^t$.  The cited theorem assumes the averaged
    65	correlation estimate
    66	\[
    67	  \E_{u,v}
    68	  \operatorname{Re}\operatorname{Tr}\!\left(
    69	    O^u O^v O^{u+v}\rho\right) \geq 1-\delta.
    70	\]
    71	Its Fourier--Naimark argument produces an auxiliary space $H'$, a unit vector
    72	$\mathrm{anc}\in H'$, and binary observables $L^u$ on $H\otimes H'$ satisfying,
    73	with
    74	$\rho'=\rho\otimes|\mathrm{anc}\rangle\langle\mathrm{anc}|$,
    75	\[
    76	  L^uL^v=L^{u+v}
    77	  \quad\text{for every }u,v.
    78	\]
    79	Moreover,
    80	\[
    81	  \E_{u}
    82	  \operatorname{Tr}\!\left((L^u-O^u\otimes I_{H'})^\dagger
    83	    (L^u-O^u\otimes I_{H'})\,\rho'\right)\leq2\delta.
    84	\]
    85	Equivalently, if $d^{\mathrm{bin}}_{\rho'}$ denotes the distance between the
    86	binary projective measurements associated with the two observables, then
    87	\[
    88	  \E_{u}
    89	  d^{\mathrm{bin}}_{\rho'}(L^u,O^u\otimes I_{H'})^2\leq\delta.
    90	\]
    91	The provider prints $\delta$ for the first, operator-distance bound.  Its
    92	calculation instead proves the second, measurement-distance bound, which is
    93	one half of the squared operator distance.  The factor-of-two discrepancy and
    94	a counterexample to the printed operator bound are given in
    95	\path{docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_linearity-distance-normalization.tex}, tracked in
    96	\ghissue{124}.
    97	In particular, $L^0=I$: exact linearity gives $(L^0)^2=L^0$, while an
    98	observable is invertible.
    99	
   100	\paragraph{Common-ancilla form.}
   101	The auxiliary space and vector do not depend on $H$, $\rho$, $\delta$, or the
   102	family $O$.  For every $t\geq1$ there are a Hilbert space $H'_t$ of dimension
   103	$2^t+1$ and a unit vector $\mathrm{anc}_t\in H'_t$ such that, for every
   104	finite-dimensional $H$, every density operator $\rho$ on $H$, every
   105	$\delta\geq0$, and every family of binary observables $O^u$ on $H$ satisfying
   106	the correlation estimate, there are exactly linear binary observables $L^u$ on
   107	$H\otimes H'_t$ with the two conclusions displayed above for
   108	$\rho'=\rho\otimes|\mathrm{anc}_t\rangle\langle\mathrm{anc}_t|$.  Indeed,
   109	in the proof the space $H'_t$ has an orthonormal basis indexed by
   110	$\F_2^t\sqcup\{\bot\}$, the vector $\mathrm{anc}_t$ is the basis vector of
   111	$\bot$, and the projective measurement $\{C^v\}$ dilating the Fourier-square
   112	POVM $B^v=(\widehat{O}^v)^2$ is realized on $H\otimes H'_t$ by the
   113	one-measurement Naimark construction, whatever $H$, $\rho$, and $O$ are.
   114	
   115	\paragraph{The statement proved for the combined point measurements.}
   116	Let $\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},X),x}_a$ and $\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},Z),z}_b$,
   117	$a,b\in\F_q$, be the expanded point measurements, projective measurements on
   118	$\mathcal{H}\otimes(\C^q)^{\otimes M}$.  Write $\delta_{\mathrm{Anticom}}(\eps)$ for
   119	the approximate-commutation error of their binary refinements and $\eps$ for
   120	their self-consistency error, both on average over the points and with respect
   121	to the expanded state $|\hat\psi\rangle$.  Then, for every pair $(x,z)$, the
   122	sandwich
   123	\[
   124	  R^{x,z}_{a,b}
   125	  \,=\,\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},Z),z}_b\,
   126	  \hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},X),x}_a\,
   127	  \hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},Z),z}_b ,
   128	  \qquad a,b\in\F_q ,
   129	\]
   130	is a POVM on the same space, and there is a universal constant $C$ such that,
   131	on average over uniformly random $x,z\in\F_q^m$ and for either bipartition
   132	scheme of the six registers,
   133	\[
   134	  \sum_{a,b}\bigl\|\bigl(R^{x,z}_{a,b}
   135	    -\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},Z),z}_b\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},X),x}_a\bigr)
   136	    |\hat\psi\rangle\bigr\|^2
   137	  \leq C\,\delta_{\mathrm{Anticom}} ,
   138	  \qquad
   139	  \sum_{(a,b)\neq(a',b')}
   140	  \langle\hat\psi|\,(R^{x,z}_{a,b})_{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'}\,
   141	  (R^{x,z}_{a',b'})_{\mathsf{B}\mathsf{A}''}\,|\hat\psi\rangle
   142	  \leq C\,(\eps+\delta_{\mathrm{Anticom}}) .
   143	\]
   144	Applying the orthonormalization lemma to $R^{x,z}$ for each fixed $(x,z)$
   145	yields projective measurements $\hat{Q}^{x,z}_{a,b}$ on
   146	$\mathcal{H}\otimes(\C^q)^{\otimes M}$ with all the conclusions of the source's
   147	Lemma~4.10 and error $\delta_Q(\eps)=O(\eps^{1/8})$.  No auxiliary space, no
   148	linearity theorem, and no Fourier averaging over binary refinements enter.

   150	\section{Comparison with the quoted statement}
   151	
   152	Lines~711--725 of
   153	\path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex} quote the
   154	linearity theorem.  The displayed hypothesis correctly averages over both
   155	group variables.  The displayed conclusion, however, says that the corrected
   156	observable is close for every $u$, whereas Theorem~10 of the cited work gives
   157	closeness only on average over $u$ \cite{Natarajan2017Linearity}.  The
   158	quotation also inserts $\delta\leq1$, which is absent from the provider theorem
   159	and would unnecessarily obstruct applying it with a fiber's actual defect, and
   160	it appends the assertion at the identity, which follows from exact linearity as
   161	above.  These three are the differences between the quotation and the cited
   162	statement.
   163	
   164	The factor of two is not one of them.  The provider's equation~(3) proves the
   165	bound $\delta$ for binary-measurement distance; under the operator-distance
   166	convention displayed above this is the bound $2\delta$, and it is the
   167	provider's own Theorem~10 that prints $\delta$ for the operator distance.  The
   168	quotation states its conclusion in the relation $\approx_\delta$, which asserts
   169	only an $O(\delta)$ bound and therefore absorbs the constant factor instead of
   170	reproducing the erroneous one.  The normalization defect and its counterexample
   171	are the provider's and are treated in
   172	\path{docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_linearity-distance-normalization.tex}.
   173	
   174	Lines~825--832 construct the family $O^{x,z,r,s}$ and establish approximate
   175	linearity only after averaging over $x,z,r,r',s,s'$.  They then apply the
   176	single-family theorem separately for every $(x,z)$ and state that
   177	``by assuming that $|\hat\psi\rangle$ has sufficiently many ancilla zero
   178	qubits, we do not need to extend the state further.''  Two things are implicit
   179	here: that the auxiliary spaces returned for different pairs $(x,z)$ can be
   180	taken to be one and the same, and that the strategy space already contains
   181	that auxiliary space in a zero state.  The next section treats both.

   183	\section{The common-ancilla obligation and the padding assumption}
   184	
   185	\paragraph{The ancilla is uniform.}
   186	The first implicit point is settled by the common-ancilla form of the theorem
   187	stated in Section~2: the auxiliary space $H'_t$ and the vector
   188	$\mathrm{anc}_t$ are functions of $t=2\log_2 q$ alone.  Applying the theorem
   189	to the family $(r,s)\mapsto O^{x,z,r,s}$ for each pair $(x,z)$ therefore
   190	produces exactly linear observables $L^{x,z,r,s}$, all acting on the one space
   191	$\mathcal{H}\otimes(\C^q)^{\otimes M}\otimes H'_t$, all compared with the ampliated
   192	originals in the one state
   193	$|\hat\psi\rangle\otimes|\mathrm{anc}_t\rangle$.  Averaging the fiberwise
   194	bounds over $(x,z)$ is then legitimate, and the finite common-extension
   195	construction envisaged in the earlier version of this note (embedding
   196	fiber-dependent spaces into a common one) is unnecessary.
   197	
   198	\paragraph{The padding is essential and is not available.}
   199	The second implicit point is a genuine assumption on the strategy, not a
   200	property of the theorem.  Write $H=\mathcal{H}\otimes(\C^q)^{\otimes M}$.  The
   201	exactly linear family lives on $H\otimes H'_t$, and the operator
   202	$\hat{Q}^{x,z}_{a,b}=\E_{r,s}(-1)^{\tr(ra+sb)}L^{x,z,r,s}$ of the source is a
   203	projector on $H\otimes H'_t$.  The source needs it on $H$, and obtains this
   204	by assuming $\mathcal{H}=\mathcal{H}_0\otimes H'_t$ with $|\hat\psi\rangle$ supported on
   205	$|\mathrm{anc}_t\rangle$ in the second factor and every measurement of the
   206	strategy acting as the identity there.  Every strategy admits a padded
   207	extension through local isometric embeddings, so the assumption costs nothing for the source's
   208	final theorem, which is stated up to local isometries.  It does, however,
   209	change the statement of Lemma~4.10: read on a fixed strategy, the source's
   210	proof establishes the lemma only for padded strategies, which is a
   211	conditional statement of exactly the kind excluded from paper-facing
   212	declarations by \path{docs/paper-gaps/proof-gap-protocol.tex}.
   213	
   214	The ancilla cannot be removed afterwards.  Compressing the family along the
   215	ancilla returns the Fourier-square POVM: since $\{C^v\}$ dilates
   216	$\{B^v\}$, one has
   217	$\langle\mathrm{anc}_t|\,\hat{Q}^{x,z}_{a,b}\,|\mathrm{anc}_t\rangle
   218	=\E_{r,s}(-1)^{\tr(ra+sb)}\sum_v(-1)^{v\cdot(r,s)}B^v
   219	=B^{(a,b)}=\bigl(\widehat{O}^{x,z,(a,b)}\bigr)^2$,
   220	where $\widehat{O}^{x,z,(a,b)}=\E_{r,s}(-1)^{\tr(ra+sb)}O^{x,z,r,s}$ is the
   221	Fourier coefficient of the original family.  This is a POVM on $H$, but it is
   222	projective only when the original family is already exactly linear.  Thus no
   223	choice of ancilla and no compression produces the projective measurement the
   224	lemma asserts from the output of the linearity theorem; the projectivity is
   225	purchased precisely by the extra dimensions.
   226	
   227	\paragraph{A direct construction on the original space.}
   228	The formal statement of Lemma~4.10 quantifies over every projective strategy
   229	and asks for projective measurements on $H$ for that strategy.  It is proved
   230	as stated, by observing that the passage through binary refinements, exact
   231	linearity, and Fourier averaging can be bypassed.  The source uses the binary
   232	refinements $\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u,r}_b$ because the approximate
   233	commutation of the expanded point projections is established for them
   234	(Lemma~4.9(2) of the source), and the linearity theorem is the device that
   235	returns from $\F_2$-valued to $\F_q$-valued outcomes.  But the commutation
   236	estimate transfers to the $\F_q$-valued measurements exactly.  With
   237	$\chi(a)=(-1)^{\tr(a)}$ and $\hat{W}^r(u)$ the expanded observables, the
   238	definitions give
   239	$\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},X),x}_a=\E_r\chi(ar)\hat{X}^r(x)$ and
   240	$\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},Z),z}_b=\E_s\chi(bs)\hat{Z}^s(z)$, hence
   241	\[
   242	  \bigl[\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},X),x}_a,\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},Z),z}_b\bigr]
   243	  =\E_{r,s}\,\chi(ar)\chi(bs)\,
   244	  \bigl[\hat{X}^r(x),\hat{Z}^s(z)\bigr] .
   245	\]
   246	Parseval's identity for the characters $a\mapsto\chi(ar)$ of $\F_q$, which are
   247	orthogonal, states that for any vectors $v_{r,s}$,
   248	\[
   249	  \sum_{a,b\in\F_q}
   250	  \Bigl\|\E_{r,s}\chi(ar)\chi(bs)\,v_{r,s}\Bigr\|^2
   251	  \,=\,\E_{r,s}\,\|v_{r,s}\|^2 ,
   252	\]
   253	so that, for every placement of the operators on the expanded state,
   254	\[
   255	  \E_{x,z}\sum_{a,b}
   256	  \bigl\|\bigl[\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},X),x}_a,
   257	    \hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},Z),z}_b\bigr]|\hat\psi\rangle\bigr\|^2
   258	  =\E_{x,z,r,s}
   259	  \bigl\|\bigl[\hat{X}^r(x),\hat{Z}^s(z)\bigr]|\hat\psi\rangle\bigr\|^2
   260	  =4\,\E_{\omega}\sum_{b,b'}
   261	  \bigl\|\bigl[\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},X),x,r}_b,
   262	    \hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},Z),z,s}_{b'}\bigr]|\hat\psi\rangle\bigr\|^2 ,
   263	\]
   264	the last equality because the binary refinements are
   265	$\tfrac12(I\pm\hat{W}^r(u))$.  The right-hand side is
   266	$O(\delta_{\mathrm{Anticom}})$ by the source's Lemma~4.9.  There is no loss
   267	in $q$; an application of Jensen's inequality in place of Parseval would lose
   268	a factor $q^2$ and would not give a polynomial in $\eps$.
   269	
   270	Given this, the source's first step goes through verbatim with $\F_q$-valued
   271	outcomes.  The sandwich $R^{x,z}_{a,b}$ of Section~2 is a POVM, and
   272	$R^{x,z}_{a,b}-\hat{M}^Z_b\hat{M}^X_a=\hat{M}^Z_b[\hat{M}^X_a,\hat{M}^Z_b]$
   273	with $\hat{M}^Z_b$ a contraction, so $R^{x,z}$ is
   274	$O(\delta_{\mathrm{Anticom}})$-close to the ordered product.  For the
   275	self-consistency of $R^{x,z}$ between the placements
   276	$\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'$ and $\mathsf{B}\mathsf{A}''$ an exact identity replaces
   277	the source's Cauchy--Schwarz chain.  Writing $P_1,P_2$ for the two placements
   278	of an operator $P$, $D^W_c=(\hat{M}^W_c)_1-(\hat{M}^W_c)_2$, and
   279	$w_b=(\hat{M}^Z_b)_1(\hat{M}^Z_b)_2|\hat\psi\rangle$, the placements commute
   280	and the effects are Hermitian projectors, so
   281	\[
   282	  \sum_{(a,b)\neq(a',b')}
   283	  \langle\hat\psi|(R^{x,z}_{a,b})_1(R^{x,z}_{a',b'})_2|\hat\psi\rangle
   284	  \,=\,1-\sum_{a,b}\langle w_b|(\hat{M}^X_a)_1(\hat{M}^X_a)_2|w_b\rangle
   285	  \,=\,\tfrac12\sum_b\|D^Z_b|\hat\psi\rangle\|^2
   286	  +\tfrac12\sum_{a,b}\|D^X_a w_b\|^2 ,
   287	\]
   288	using twice the identity
   289	$\sum_c\langle w|P_cQ_c|w\rangle=\|w\|^2-\tfrac12\sum_c\|(P_c-Q_c)w\|^2$ for
   290	commuting projective measurements $\{P_c\}$ and $\{Q_c\}$.  Expanding
   291	$D^X_a w_b$ as
   292	$(\hat{M}^Z_b)_1(\hat{M}^Z_b)_2D^X_a|\hat\psi\rangle
   293	+(\hat{M}^Z_b)_2([\hat{M}^X_a,\hat{M}^Z_b])_1|\hat\psi\rangle
   294	-(\hat{M}^Z_b)_1([\hat{M}^X_a,\hat{M}^Z_b])_2|\hat\psi\rangle$
   295	and using that the $\hat{M}^Z_b$ are contractions summing to the identity
   296	bounds the consistency defect by
   297	$\tfrac12\sum_b\|D^Z_b\hat\psi\|^2
   298	+\tfrac32\bigl(\sum_a\|D^X_a\hat\psi\|^2+K_1+K_2\bigr)$,
   299	where $K_i$ is the squared commutator sum at placement $i$; on average over
   300	$(x,z)$ this is $O(\eps+\delta_{\mathrm{Anticom}})$.  The defect is manifestly
   301	nonnegative, being a sum of squares.
   302	
   303	The orthonormalization lemma (Lemma~4.2 of the source, with explicit constant
   304	$220\,\delta^{1/4}$ in the formalization) applied for each fixed $(x,z)$ to the
   305	POVM $R^{x,z}$ on $\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'$ against $R^{x,z}$ on
   306	$\mathsf{B}\mathsf{A}''$ produces a projective measurement
   307	$\hat{Q}^{x,z}_{a,b}$ on $H$ with
   308	$\sum_{a,b}\|((\hat{Q}^{x,z}_{a,b}-R^{x,z}_{a,b})_{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'})
   309	\hat\psi\|^2\leq220\,c_{x,z}^{1/4}$, where $c_{x,z}$ is the bound on the
   310	defect just obtained; since $x\mapsto x^{1/4}$ is concave,
   311	$\E_{x,z}c_{x,z}^{1/4}\leq(\E_{x,z}c_{x,z})^{1/4}$, which is
   312	$O(\eps^{1/8})$.  The measurement for Bob's side is obtained in the same way
   313	from the bipartition $\mathsf{B}\mathsf{A}''\mid\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'
   314	\mathsf{B}'\mathsf{B}''$.  The remaining conclusions of Lemma~4.10 are the
   315	triangle inequality along
   316	$\hat{Q}\approx R\approx\hat{M}^Z\hat{M}^X\approx\hat{M}^X\hat{M}^Z$, together
   317	with the consistency of the ordered products across opposite placements,
   318	$(\hat{M}^Z_b\hat{M}^X_a)_1\approx(\hat{M}^X_a\hat{M}^Z_b)_2$, which follows
   319	from the self-consistency of each factor and the contraction property of the
   320	other, exactly as in the source's calculation.  The symmetric equivalents on
   321	$\mathsf{B}\mathsf{B}'$ and $\mathsf{A}\mathsf{B}''$ do not require a symmetric
   322	strategy: the permutation of the six registers that exchanges
   323	$\mathsf{A}'\leftrightarrow\mathsf{B}''$ and
   324	$\mathsf{A}''\leftrightarrow\mathsf{B}'$ fixes $|\hat\psi\rangle$, because
   325	each EPR vector is symmetric, and carries the placement
   326	$\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'$ to $\mathsf{A}\mathsf{B}''$ and
   327	$\mathsf{B}\mathsf{A}''$ to $\mathsf{B}\mathsf{B}'$, so every squared distance
   328	on one placement equals the same squared distance on its image.

   375	\section{Conclusion}
   376	
   377	The quotation changes averaged closeness to pointwise closeness, inserts an
   378	unnecessary upper bound on $\delta$, and appends an assertion at the identity
   379	that is derivable from exact linearity.  It does not reproduce the provider's
   380	factor-of-two normalization defect, since it states its conclusion in a
   381	relation that absorbs constant factors; that defect is the provider's own and
   382	is treated separately.  The single-family theorem is proved with mean squared
   383	operator error at most $2\delta$, equivalently mean squared binary-measurement
   384	error at most $\delta$, and its ancilla depends only on the index length, so
   385	the fiberwise application is uniform.  What the source additionally assumes,
   386	zero-state padding of the strategy, is not a property of an arbitrary
   387	projective strategy and cannot be dispensed with in the source's route, since
   388	the ancilla is what makes the Fourier-averaged family projective.  The combined
   389	point measurements are therefore constructed on the original space directly:
   390	Parseval's identity transfers the approximate commutation to the
   391	$\F_q$-valued point measurements without loss, the sandwich POVM is then
   392	approximately self-consistent, and the orthonormalization lemma makes it
   393	projective with error $O(\eps^{1/8})$.

`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:160-190`. -/
inductive PlayerSide where
  | alice
  | bob
  deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Inhabited, Fintype

/-- A projective strategy satisfying the winning premise used throughout
Section `sec:commutation`. The structure retains the distinct player spaces and
measurement families of `Strategy`. Paper
`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:160-172`; blueprint
`sec:commutation`. -/
structure ProjectiveSetting (P : AdmissibleParams) (ε : ℝ) where
  toStrategy : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P)
  isProjective : toStrategy.IsProjective
  win : 1 - ε ≤ toStrategy.value

namespace ProjectiveSetting

variable {P : AdmissibleParams} {ε : ℝ}

/-- The local Hilbert-space index type on a specified player side. It indexes
the side-qualified operators at paper
`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:174-190`. -/
def LocalSpace (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) : PlayerSide → Type
  | .alice => S.toStrategy.ιA
  | .bob => S.toStrategy.ιB

instance localSpaceFintype (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide) :
    Fintype (S.LocalSpace side) := by
  cases side <;> simp only [LocalSpace] <;> infer_instance

instance localSpaceDecidableEq (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide) :
    DecidableEq (S.LocalSpace side) := by
  cases side <;> simp only [LocalSpace] <;> infer_instance

/-- Select the strategy measurement before outcome postprocessing on one
player side. This is the heterogeneous interpretation of the shared symbol `M` at
paper `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:160-184`. -/
def strategyMeasurement (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide)
    (question : PauliQuestion P) :
    Measurement (PauliAnswer P) (S.LocalSpace side) := by
  cases side with
  | alice => exact S.toStrategy.A question
  | bob => exact S.toStrategy.B question

/-- Embed a point into the full Pauli question space in basis `W`. This is the
point-question content from `def:pauli-question-distribution`, paper
`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:997-1008`, blueprint

rcases h with ⟨rfl, rfl, rfl⟩
          rfl

/-- Directly indexed line descriptions form a finite type. -/
noncomputable instance directLineDescFintype (D : DirectLdParams) :
    Fintype (DirectLineDesc D) :=
  Fintype.ofInjective (directLineDescCode D) (directLineDescCode_injective D)

/-! ## Combined point and line measurements -/

/-- Projective joint point measurements and their ordered consistency
guarantees from `lem:qld-4-10`, paper lines 689--709.  The `XZ` and `ZX`
products are retained as distinct fields. -/
structure CombinedPointsWitness {P : AdmissibleParams} {ε : ℝ}
    (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (δ : ℝ) where
  /-- The complete joint measurement on each player's expanded local space. -/
  Q : (side : PlayerSide) ->
    (Fin P.m -> PauliScalar P) ->
    (Fin P.m -> PauliScalar P) ->
    Measurement (PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P) (S.ExpandedLocalSpace side)
  /-- Every joint point measurement is projective. -/
  projective : ∀ side x z, Measurement.IsProjective (Q side x z)
  /-- Joint point measurements agree across every directed opposite placement. -/
  self_consistent : ∀ p1 p2 : Placement, p1.IsOpposite p2 ->
    opFamilyDistSq
      (uniformDistribution
        ((Fin P.m -> PauliScalar P) × (Fin P.m -> PauliScalar P)))
      (fun xz ab => S.place p1 ((Q p1.side xz.1 xz.2).effect ab))
      (fun xz ab => S.place p2 ((Q p2.side xz.1 xz.2).effect ab))
      S.psiHat <= δ
  /-- Joint point measurements are close to the ordered `X`-then-`Z` product. -/
  consistent_XZ : ∀ p1 p2 : Placement, p1.IsOpposite p2 ->
    opFamilyDistSq
      (uniformDistribution
        ((Fin P.m -> PauliScalar P) × (Fin P.m -> PauliScalar P)))
      (fun xz ab => S.place p1 ((Q p1.side xz.1 xz.2).effect ab))
      (fun xz ab => S.place p2
        ((S.pointMeasExp p2.side .X xz.1).effect ab.1 *
          (S.pointMeasExp p2.side .Z xz.2).effect ab.2))
      S.psiHat <= δ
  /-- Joint point measurements are close to the ordered `Z`-then-`X` product. -/
  consistent_ZX : ∀ p1 p2 : Placement, p1.IsOpposite p2 ->
    opFamilyDistSq
      (uniformDistribution
        ((Fin P.m -> PauliScalar P) × (Fin P.m -> PauliScalar P)))
      (fun xz ab => S.place p1 ((Q p1.side xz.1 xz.2).effect ab))
      (fun xz ab => S.place p2
        ((S.pointMeasExp p2.side .Z xz.2).effect ab.2 *
          (S.pointMeasExp p2.side .X xz.1).effect ab.1))
      S.psiHat <= δ

/-- Joint line measurements and their evaluation consistency from
`lem:qld-xz-lines`, paper lines 882--894.  Evaluation uses explicit `Option`
outcomes, including the class of answers not determined at the sampled point. -/
structure CombinedLinesWitness {P : AdmissibleParams} {ε δQ : ℝ}
    (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (points : CombinedPointsWitness S δQ)
    (δ : ℝ) where
  /-- The complete paired-line measurement on each expanded local space. -/
  T : (side : PlayerSide) ->
    LineDesc P.toLdParams -> LineDesc P.toLdParams ->
    Measurement
      (DegPoly P.toLdParams (P.m * P.d) ×
        DegPoly P.toLdParams (P.m * P.d))
      (S.ExpandedLocalSpace side)
  /-- On an axis-parallel X line, outcomes outside degree `d` have zero effect. -/
  axis_degree_X : ∀ side lineX lineZ fX fZ,
    lineX.kind = .axis -> Not (DegPoly.FitsDegree P.d fX) ->
      (T side lineX lineZ).effect (fX, fZ) = 0
  /-- On an axis-parallel Z line, outcomes outside degree `d` have zero effect. -/
  axis_degree_Z : ∀ side lineX lineZ fX fZ,
    lineZ.kind = .axis -> Not (DegPoly.FitsDegree P.d fZ) ->
      (T side lineX lineZ).effect (fX, fZ) = 0
  /-- Evaluated line pairs are consistent with the completed point-pair
  measurement on every directed opposite placement. -/
  consistent : ∀ p1 p2 : Placement, p1.IsOpposite p2 ->
    consistencyDefect
      (Distribution.prod (linePointDist P.toLdParams)
        (linePointDist P.toLdParams))
      (fun sample answer => S.place p1
        (((T p1.side sample.1.1 sample.2.1).postprocess fun fs =>
          (evalOpt sample.1.1 sample.1.2 fs.1,
            evalOpt sample.2.1 sample.2.2 fs.2)).effect answer))
      (fun sample answer => S.place p2
        (((points.Q p2.side sample.1.2 sample.2.2).postprocess fun ab =>
          (some ab.1, some ab.2)).effect answer))
      S.psiHat <= δ

have hCZ :
        qSDD Ψ (leftPlacedSubMeas (ιB := ιB) C.toSubMeas)
          (leftPlacedSubMeas (ιB := ιB) Z.toSubMeas) ≤ 1 :=

    have hZC :

    refine ⟨C, ?_⟩

              (leftPlacedSubMeas (ιB := ιB) C.toSubMeas)) :=
        MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.questionSDD_triangle Ψ
          (leftPlacedSubMeas (ιB := ιB) A.toSubMeas)
          (leftPlacedSubMeas (ιB := ιB) Z.toSubMeas)
          (leftPlacedSubMeas (ιB := ιB) C.toSubMeas)
      _ ≤ 4 := by linarith
      _ ≤ 220 * t := by nlinarith

/-- A consistent pair of POVMs admits an Alice-side projective rounding with
the explicit dimension-independent error `220 * δ^(1/4)`. -/
theorem projective_rounding_with_explicit_constant {ιA ιB α : Type*}
    [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB)) (hψ : ‖ψ‖ = 1)
    (Q : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α ιA)
    (R : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α ιB) (δ : Error) (hδ : 0 ≤ δ)
    (hcons : consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution Unit)
      (fun _ a => heteroKron (Q.effect a) 1)
      (fun _ a => heteroKron 1 (R.effect a)) ψ ≤ δ) :
    ∃ Pm : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α ιA,
      MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective Pm ∧
      opFamilyDistSq (uniformDistribution Unit)
        (fun _ a => heteroKron (Pm.effect a) 1)
        (fun _ a => heteroKron (Q.effect a) 1) ψ ≤
          220 * Real.rpow δ (1 / 4 : Error) := by
  have hι : Nonempty (ιA × ιB) := by
    by_contra hempty
    letI : IsEmpty (ιA × ιB) := not_nonempty_iff.mp hempty
    have hzero : ψ = 0 := Subsingleton.elim _ _
    rw [hzero, norm_zero] at hψ
    norm_num at hψ
  haveI : Nonempty ιA := ⟨(Classical.choice hι).1⟩
  haveI : Nonempty ιB := ⟨(Classical.choice hι).2⟩
  have hα : Nonempty α := round_measurement_outcome_nonempty Q
  letI : Nonempty α := hα
  let a₀ : α := Classical.choice hα
  let Ψ : PureState (ιA × ιB) := roundPureState ψ hψ
  let HA : FiniteHilbertSpace := roundFiniteHilbertSpace ιA
  let HB : FiniteHilbertSpace := roundFiniteHilbertSpace ιB
  let A : MIPStarRE.LDT.Measurement α ιA :=
    MatrixMeasurement.toMeasurement (H := HA) Q
  let B : MIPStarRE.LDT.Measurement α ιB :=
    MatrixMeasurement.toMeasurement (H := HB) R
  have hCons : ConsRel (Ψ : QuantumState (ιA × ιB)) (uniformDistribution Unit)
      (constSubMeasFamily A.toSubMeas) (constSubMeasFamily B.toSubMeas) δ := by
    simpa [Ψ, HA, HB, A, B] using
      round_consRel_of_consistencyDefect ψ hψ Q R δ hcons
  obtain ⟨C, hC⟩ := round_projective_ldt (Ψ : QuantumState (ιA × ιB))
    Ψ.toQuantumState_isNormalized A B a₀ δ hδ hCons
  let Pm : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α ιA :=
    MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.ofSumEqOne C.outcome C.outcome_pos <| by
      rw [C.sum_eq_total, C.total_eq_one]
  have hPm_projective : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective Pm := by
    intro a
    change IsProj (C.outcome a)
    exact
      { isIdempotentElem := C.proj a
        isSelfAdjoint :=
          (Matrix.nonneg_iff_posSemidef.mp (C.outcome_pos a)).isHermitian.eq }
  refine ⟨Pm, hPm_projective, ?_⟩
  have hdist :
      opFamilyDistSq (uniformDistribution Unit)
          (fun _ a => heteroKron (Pm.effect a) 1)
          (fun _ a => heteroKron (Q.effect a) 1) ψ =
        qSDD (Ψ : QuantumState (ιA × ιB))
          (leftPlacedSubMeas (ιB := ιB) C.toSubMeas)
          (leftPlacedSubMeas (ιB := ιB) A.toSubMeas) := by
    unfold opFamilyDistSq
    rw [show avgOver (uniformDistribution Unit)
        (fun _ => ∑ a : α,
          ‖applyOperatorToState
            (heteroKron (Pm.effect a) 1 - heteroKron (Q.effect a) 1) ψ‖ ^ 2) =
        ∑ a : α,
          ‖applyOperatorToState
            (heteroKron (Pm.effect a) 1 - heteroKron (Q.effect a) 1) ψ‖ ^ 2 by
      simp [avgOver, uniformDistribution]]

calc (2 : ℂ)⁻¹ • (1 + phaseSign b • A) *
        ((2 : ℂ)⁻¹ • (1 + phaseSign b' • B)) -
        (2 : ℂ)⁻¹ • (1 + phaseSign b' • B) *
          ((2 : ℂ)⁻¹ • (1 + phaseSign b • A))
      = (4 : ℂ)⁻¹ • ((1 + phaseSign b • A) * (1 + phaseSign b' • B) -
          (1 + phaseSign b' • B) * (1 + phaseSign b • A)) := by
        rw [smul_mul_assoc, mul_smul_comm, smul_smul, smul_mul_assoc,
          mul_smul_comm, smul_smul, ← smul_sub]
        norm_num
    _ = ((4 : ℂ)⁻¹ * (phaseSign b * phaseSign b')) • (A * B - B * A) := by
        rw [hexp, smul_smul]

/-! ## The approximate commutation on each placement -/

/-- The placement of a scalar multiple is the scalar multiple of the
placement. Paper `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:420-450`,
blueprint `ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:1002-1031`. -/
theorem place_smul (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (p : Placement) (c : ℂ)
    (O : Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace p.side)) :
    S.place p (c • O) = c • S.place p O := by
  ext i j
  cases p <;> simp only [place, Matrix.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul] <;> ring

/-- The twisted commutator of the point observables is small on average, on
either player side. This packages both orientations of
`eq:pts-obs-commutation`; paper
`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:309-354`, blueprint
`ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:761-794`. -/
theorem exists_twistedCommutator_avg_le :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 1 ≤ C ∧
      ∀ (P : AdmissibleParams) (ε : ℝ) (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
        (side : PlayerSide), 0 ≤ ε →
      avgOver (uniformDistribution (PauliTuple P)) (fun ω =>
        ‖applyOperatorToState (S.placeStrategySide side (S.twistedCommutator side ω))
          S.toStrategy.ψ‖ ^ 2) ≤ C * Real.sqrt ε := by
  obtain ⟨C₁, hC₁, h₁⟩ := pointObs_twisted_commutation
  obtain ⟨C₂, hC₂, h₂⟩ := pointObs_twisted_commutation_interchanged
  refine ⟨C₁ + C₂, by linarith, ?_⟩
  intro P ε S side hε
  have hs : (0 : ℝ) ≤ Real.sqrt ε := Real.sqrt_nonneg ε
  cases side with
  | alice =>
      have h := h₁ P ε S hε
      rw [WinImplications.opDistSq_eq_avgOver] at h
      refine le_trans (le_of_eq ?_) (le_trans h ?_)
      · refine avgOver_congr _ _ _ (fun ω => ?_)
        have hop : S.placeStrategySide .alice (S.twistedCommutator .alice ω) =
            heteroKron (S.pointObs .alice .X ω.2.2.1 ω.1 *
                S.pointObs .alice .Z ω.2.2.2 ω.2.1)
                (1 : Op S.toStrategy.ιB) -
              phaseSign (gammaValue P ω.1 ω.2.1 ω.2.2.1 ω.2.2.2) •
                heteroKron (S.pointObs .alice .Z ω.2.2.2 ω.2.1 *
                  S.pointObs .alice .X ω.2.2.1 ω.1) 1 := by
          have h1 : heteroKron (S.twistedCommutator .alice ω)
              (1 : Op S.toStrategy.ιB) =
              heteroKron (S.pointObs .alice .X ω.2.2.1 ω.1 *
                S.pointObs .alice .Z ω.2.2.2 ω.2.1) 1 -
                heteroKron
                  (phaseSign (gammaValue P ω.1 ω.2.1 ω.2.2.1 ω.2.2.2) •
                    (S.pointObs .alice .Z ω.2.2.2 ω.2.1 *
                      S.pointObs .alice .X ω.2.2.1 ω.1)) 1 :=
            heteroKron_sub_left _ _ _
          rw [← WinImplications.heteroKron_smul_left]
          exact h1
        rw [hop]
        rfl
      · nlinarith
  | bob =>
      have h := h₂ P ε S hε
      rw [WinImplications.opDistSq_eq_avgOver] at h
      refine le_trans (le_of_eq ?_) (le_trans h ?_)
      · refine avgOver_congr _ _ _ (fun ω => ?_)
        have hop : S.placeStrategySide .bob (S.twistedCommutator .bob ω) =
            heteroKron (1 : Op S.toStrategy.ιA)
                (S.pointObs .bob .X ω.2.2.1 ω.1 *
                  S.pointObs .bob .Z ω.2.2.2 ω.2.1) -
              phaseSign (gammaValue P ω.1 ω.2.1 ω.2.2.1 ω.2.2.2) •
                heteroKron 1 (S.pointObs .bob .Z ω.2.2.2 ω.2.1 *
                  S.pointObs .bob .X ω.2.2.1 ω.1) := by
          have h1 : heteroKron (1 : Op S.toStrategy.ιA)
              (S.twistedCommutator .bob ω) =
              heteroKron 1 (S.pointObs .bob .X ω.2.2.1 ω.1 *
                S.pointObs .bob .Z ω.2.2.2 ω.2.1) -
                heteroKron 1
                  (phaseSign (gammaValue P ω.1 ω.2.1 ω.2.2.1 ω.2.2.2) •
                    (S.pointObs .bob .Z ω.2.2.2 ω.2.1 *
                      S.pointObs .bob .X ω.2.2.1 ω.1)) :=
            heteroKron_sub_right _ _ _
          rw [← MagicSquareRigidity.heteroKron_smul_right]
          exact h1
        rw [hop]
        rfl
      · nlinarith

/-- Trace-coarse-grained expanded point projections approximately commute on
each of the four register placements. This is item 2 of `lem:qld-comm-cons`,
paper `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:466-505`, blueprint
`ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:1164-1175`. -/
theorem expPointTrace_comm_proof :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 1 ≤ C ∧
      ∀ (P : AdmissibleParams) (ε : ℝ) (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)

(∃ C : ℝ, 1 ≤ C ∧
    ∀ (P : AdmissibleParams) (ε : ℝ) (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
      (p : Placement),
      opFamilyDistSq (uniformDistribution (PauliTuple P))
        (fun ω (bits : ZMod 2 × ZMod 2) => S.place p
          ((S.expPointTrace p.side .X ω.1 ω.2.2.1).effect bits.1 *
            (S.expPointTrace p.side .Z ω.2.1 ω.2.2.2).effect bits.2))
        (fun ω (bits : ZMod 2 × ZMod 2) => S.place p
          ((S.expPointTrace p.side .Z ω.2.1 ω.2.2.2).effect bits.2 *
            (S.expPointTrace p.side .X ω.1 ω.2.2.1).effect bits.1))
        S.psiHat ≤ C * δ ε)

/-- Expanded point measurements are self-consistent for each of the four
directed opposite-placement pairs. The universal constant precedes all test
parameters and strategies. This is item 1 of `lem:qld-comm-cons`, paper
`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:455-465`, blueprint
`lem:qld-comm-cons`. -/
theorem expPoint_self_cons :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 1 ≤ C ∧
      ∀ (P : AdmissibleParams) (ε : ℝ) (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
        (p₁ p₂ : Placement), p₁.IsOpposite p₂ →
        ∀ W : PauliKind,
          opFamilyDistSq (uniformDistribution (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P))
            (fun u a => S.place p₁
              ((S.pointMeasExp p₁.side W u).effect a))
            (fun u a => S.place p₂
              ((S.pointMeasExp p₂.side W u).effect a))
            S.psiHat ≤ C * ε := by
  refine ⟨2 * (Fintype.card PauliEdge : ℝ), ?_, ?_⟩
  · have hcard : (1 : ℝ) ≤ Fintype.card PauliEdge := by
      exact_mod_cast (Fintype.card_pos : 0 < Fintype.card PauliEdge)
    linarith
  intro P ε S p₁ p₂ hopp W
  cases p₁ <;> cases p₂ <;> simp only [Placement.IsOpposite] at hopp
  · simpa only [Placement.side, mul_assoc] using
      ProjectiveSetting.expPointDist_aaBa_le S W
  · rw [DistanceCalculus.opFamilyDistSq_symm]
    simpa only [Placement.side, mul_assoc] using
      ProjectiveSetting.expPointDist_aaBa_le S W
  · rw [DistanceCalculus.opFamilyDistSq_symm]
    simpa only [Placement.side, mul_assoc] using
      ProjectiveSetting.expPointDist_abBb_le S W
  · simpa only [Placement.side, mul_assoc] using
      ProjectiveSetting.expPointDist_abBb_le S W

/-- Trace-coarse-grained expanded point projections approximately commute on
each of `AA'`, `BA''`, `BB'`, and `AB''`. The universal constant precedes all
test parameters and strategies. This is item 2 of `lem:qld-comm-cons`, paper
`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:466-505`, blueprint
`lem:qld-comm-cons`. -/
theorem expPointTrace_comm :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 1 ≤ C ∧
      ∀ (P : AdmissibleParams) (ε : ℝ) (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
        (p : Placement),
        opFamilyDistSq (uniformDistribution (PauliTuple P))
          (fun ω (bits : ZMod 2 × ZMod 2) => S.place p
            ((S.expPointTrace p.side .X ω.1 ω.2.2.1).effect bits.1 *
              (S.expPointTrace p.side .Z ω.2.1 ω.2.2.2).effect bits.2))
          (fun ω (bits : ZMod 2 × ZMod 2) => S.place p
            ((S.expPointTrace p.side .Z ω.2.1 ω.2.2.2).effect bits.2 *
              (S.expPointTrace p.side .X ω.1 ω.2.2.1).effect bits.1))
          S.psiHat ≤ C * deltaAnticom ε :=
  ProjectiveSetting.expPointTrace_comm_proof

/-- The source's existential polynomial-error formulation, derived from the
concrete square-root bounds rather than postulated independently. This is
`lem:qld-comm-cons`, paper `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:452-505`,
blueprint `lem:qld-comm-cons`. -/
theorem exists_deltaAnticom :
    ∃ δ : ℝ → ℝ, IsPolyErr δ ∧ ExpandedPointConclusions δ := by
  refine ⟨deltaAnticom, deltaAnticom_isPolyErr, ?_⟩
  exact ⟨expPoint_self_cons, expPointTrace_comm⟩

end

/-!
# The quantum linearity theorem

This file proves the quantum linearity theorem of Natarajan and Vidick in the
form used to combine the binary observables produced in the point analysis.
A family of binary observables indexed by the Boolean cube `F_2^t`, whose
two-query linearity correlation weighted by a positive semidefinite trace-one
operator `ρ` is at least `1 - δ`, is close on average, in the state-dependent
distance weighted by `ρ ⊗ |anc⟩⟨anc|`, to an exactly linear family of binary
observables on a finite ancillary extension.

The proof assembles two results of the linearity route: the operator BLR bound
`avg_multiplicativeDefect_le_two_mul_error`, which converts the correlation
hypothesis into the bound `2δ` on the average multiplicative defect
`E_{u,u'} d_ρ(O^u O^{u'}, O^{u+u'})^2`, and Boolean representation stability
`exists_exact_boolean_representation`, which converts that defect bound into
the exactly linear family with the same average distance bound.  The notions
in which the theorem is stated are in
`MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity/Defs.lean`.

## Main results

* `exists_exactly_linear_observables`: the theorem, with the closeness measured
  by the squared state-dependent operator distance `stateDepDistSq` and the
  bound `2 * δ`.
* `exists_exactly_linear_observables_binaryObservableDistSq`: the same
  conclusion measured by the binary-measurement distance
  `binaryObservableDistSq`, with the bound `δ` intended by the source.

## References

The declaration is blueprint
`thm:linearity`.  The QPBT paper quotes
the theorem at
`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:713-725`; the
provider is Theorem 10 of Natarajan--Vidick, arXiv:1610.03574,
`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1074-1113`.  The normalization of the
distance bound is analyzed in
`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_linearity-distance-normalization.tex`.
-/

/-- The quantum linearity theorem of Natarajan--Vidick.  Let `t` be positive,
`δ ≥ 0`, `ρ` a positive semidefinite trace-one operator on a finite-dimensional
Hilbert space, and `O^u`, for `u ∈ F_2^t`, binary observables whose two-query
correlation satisfies `E_{u,u'} Re Tr(O^u O^{u'} O^{u+u'} ρ) ≥ 1 - δ`.  Then
there are a finite-dimensional ancillary Hilbert space, a unit vector `anc` in
it, and binary observables `L^u` on the tensor-product Hilbert space such that
`L^u L^{u'} = L^{u+u'}` for all `u, u'` and
`E_u d_{ρ'}(L^u, O^u ⊗ 1)^2 ≤ 2δ`, where `ρ' = ρ ⊗ |anc⟩⟨anc|`.

This is Theorem 10 of Natarajan--Vidick,
`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1074-1088`, hypothesis as in its display
(7) and conclusion as in its display (8), stated as blueprint
`thm:linearity`; the QPBT paper quotes
it at `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:713-725`.
As recorded in blueprint `rem:linearity-import`, this form
imposes no upper bound on `δ`, asserts exact linearity for every pair, and
averages closeness only over `u`.  The quotation instead adds `δ ≤ 1`, phrases
closeness pointwise under a pair quantifier, and appends `L 0 = 1`; those three
deviations are not reproduced.  The identity at zero follows from exact
linearity and the binary-observable condition.

**Local fix:** The source prints the closeness bound as `δ` for the squared
state-dependent operator distance.  Its calculation at
`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:900-912` bounds the squared distance between
the binary projective measurements of the observables, which is half the
squared operator distance, and then identifies the two quantities; the operator
bound `δ` is refuted by a four-point counterexample, and the bound established
by the Fourier--Naimark argument is `2 * δ` for `stateDepDistSq`, equivalently
`δ` for `binaryObservableDistSq`
(`exists_exactly_linear_observables_binaryObservableDistSq`).  Documented in
`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_linearity-distance-normalization.tex` and blueprint
`rem:linearity-distance-normalization`.

The proof passes the correlation hypothesis through the operator BLR bound
`avg_multiplicativeDefect_le_two_mul_error`, obtaining
`E_{u,u'} d_ρ(O^u O^{u'}, O^{u+u'})^2 ≤ 2δ`, and applies Boolean representation
stability `exists_exact_boolean_representation` with `η = 2δ`. -/
theorem exists_exactly_linear_observables {ι : Type}
    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (t : ℕ) (ht : 0 < t) (δ : ℝ) (hδ : 0 ≤ δ)
    (ρ : Op ι) (hρ : ρ.PosSemidef) (htrace : ρ.trace = 1)
    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι)
    (hO : ∀ u, IsBinaryObservable (O u))
    (hcorrelation :
      1 - δ ≤ avgOver
        (uniformDistribution
          ((Fin t → ZMod 2) × (Fin t → ZMod 2)))
        (fun pair =>
          (Matrix.trace
            (O pair.1 * O pair.2 * O (pair.1 + pair.2) * ρ)).re)) :
    ∃ (ι' : Type) (_ : Fintype ι') (_ : DecidableEq ι')
        (anc : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι'),
      ‖anc‖ = 1 ∧
        ∃ L : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op (ι × ι'),
          (∀ u, IsBinaryObservable (L u)) ∧
          (∀ u u', L u * L u' = L (u + u')) ∧
          avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin t → ZMod 2))
              (fun u => stateDepDistSq (L u)
                (heteroKron (O u) (1 : Op ι'))
                (heteroKron ρ (ancProj anc))) ≤ 2 * δ :=
  exists_exact_boolean_representation t ht (2 * δ) (by linarith) ρ hρ htrace O hO
    (avg_multiplicativeDefect_le_two_mul_error O hO ρ hρ htrace δ hcorrelation)

`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1083-1086`, in the measurement-distance

which the source's calculation is correct; see
blueprint `rem:linearity-distance-normalization` and
`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_linearity-distance-normalization.tex`.  It follows from
`exists_exactly_linear_observables` by halving, through
`binaryObservableDistSq_eq_stateDepDistSq_div_two`. -/

    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (t : ℕ) (ht : 0 < t) (δ : ℝ) (hδ : 0 ≤ δ)

steps. First we show that any set of quantum observables satisfying
linearity relations approximately in expectation can be ``rounded'' to a
nearby set of observables satisfying these relations exactly. 

\begin{theorem}
  Suppose there exist observables $\{A(a)\}_{a\in
  \{0,1\}^n}$ in $\Obs(\mH)$ acting on a state
  $\rho \in \Density(\mH)$ such that 
	\begin{equation}\label{eq:qblr-0}
	\E_{a, b} \Trho\big( A(a) A(b) A(a+b)\big) \geq 1-\delta.
	\end{equation}
	Then there exists an extended state $\rho' = \rho \otimes
  \proj{\rm{anc}} \in \Density(\mH\otimes \mH')$ and observables $\{\cA(a)\}$ in $\Obs(\mH\otimes\mH')$ such that 
	\begin{equation}\label{eq:qblr-1}
	\cA(a) \cA(b) = \cA(a+b) \quad \forall a, b \in \{0, 1\}^n\qquad \text{and}\qquad \E_a
  \DIS_{\rho'} (\cA(a), A(a))^2 \leq\delta.
	\end{equation}
\label{thm:qblr}
\end{theorem}

Here, and throughout this paper, the notation $a + b$ denotes the
bitwise XOR of $a$ and $b$, i.e. the sum of $a$ and $b$ viewed
as elements of the additive group ${\mathbb{Z}}_2^n$. We call observables
$\{\cA(a)\}$ satisfying the first set of relations in~\eqref{eq:qblr-1} \emph{exactly linear}.

\begin{proof}
For every $u\in\{0,1\}^n$ consider the Fourier transform  $\hat{A}^u =
\E_{a} (-1)^{a\cdot u} A(a)$. Define measurement operators
  $B^u = (\hat{A}^u)^2$.
By Parseval's identity, these operators form a POVM. Using Naimark's theorem there exists an ancilla space $\mH'$, $\proj{\rm anc}\in\Density(\mH')$, and a projective
measurement $\{C^u\}$ on $\mH\otimes \mH'$ that simulates $\{B^u\}$. Introduce 
observables
\[ \cA(a) = \sum_{u} (-1)^{u\cdot a} C^u. \]
From the orthogonality of the projectors $C^u$ it follows that $\cA(a)
\cA(b) = \cA(a+b)$. Write 
\begin{align*}
  \E_{a} \CON_{\rho'}(A(a), \cA(a))
  &= \frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{2}\E_{a}\Re\Tr_{\rho'}\big( A(a)\cA(a)\big)\\
	&= \frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{2}\E_{a}\Re\Big(\sum_u \Trho\big( (-1)^{u\cdot a} A(a)(\hat{A}^u)^2\big)\Big)\\
	&= \frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{2}\sum_u \Trho\big((\hat{A}^u)^3\big).
\end{align*}
To conclude, note that
  $\sum_u \Trho((\hat{A}^u)^3) =\E_{ab} \Trho(A(a) A(b) A(a + b))$, and use the assumption made in the theorem and the relation between $\CON_{\rho'}$ and $\DIS_{\rho'}^2 $.
\end{proof}

Next we exhibit a two-player game such that any strategy which succeeds with
probability at least $1 - \eps$ in the game must satisfy the assumption~\eqref{eq:qblr-0} of
Theorem~\ref{thm:qblr} for some $\delta = O(\sqrt{\eps})$.

/-- A binary observable is a Hermitian operator whose square is the identity.
This is the finite-matrix realization of `Obs(H)` in blueprint
`thm:linearity`, quoted at paper
`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:713-725`. -/
def IsBinaryObservable {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (O : Op ι) : Prop :=
  O.IsHermitian ∧ O * O = 1

namespace IsBinaryObservable

variable {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {X Y : Op ι}

/-- A binary observable is self-adjoint. -/
theorem conjTranspose_eq (hX : IsBinaryObservable X) : Xᴴ = X := hX.1

/-- A binary observable squares to the identity. -/
theorem mul_self_eq_one (hX : IsBinaryObservable X) : X * X = 1 := hX.2

/-- A binary observable is isometric: being self-adjoint and an involution, its
adjoint is its own inverse. -/
theorem isometry (hX : IsBinaryObservable X) : Xᴴ * X = 1 := by
  rw [hX.conjTranspose_eq, hX.mul_self_eq_one]

/-- The identity is a binary observable. -/
theorem one : IsBinaryObservable (1 : Op ι) :=
  ⟨Matrix.isHermitian_one, one_mul 1⟩

/-- The product of two commuting binary observables is a binary observable. -/
theorem mul (hX : IsBinaryObservable X) (hY : IsBinaryObservable Y)
    (hcomm : X * Y = Y * X) : IsBinaryObservable (X * Y) := by
  refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
  · rw [Matrix.IsHermitian, Matrix.conjTranspose_mul, hX.conjTranspose_eq,
      hY.conjTranspose_eq, ← hcomm]
  · calc X * Y * (X * Y) = X * (Y * X) * Y := by noncomm_ring
      _ = X * (X * Y) * Y := by rw [hcomm]
      _ = X * X * (Y * Y) := by noncomm_ring
      _ = 1 := by rw [hX.mul_self_eq_one, hY.mul_self_eq_one, one_mul]

end IsBinaryObservable

/-- The ampliation `O ⊗ 1` of a binary observable by the identity of a second
tensor factor is a binary observable.  This is the sense in which the original
observables `A(a)` act on the extended space in display (8) of
`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1083-1086`; it is also the way a Magic Square
observable of one player acts on the joint space of `thm:ms-rigidity`. -/
theorem isBinaryObservable_heteroKron_one {ι ι' : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    [Fintype ι'] [DecidableEq ι'] {O : Op ι} (hO : IsBinaryObservable O) :
    IsBinaryObservable (heteroKron O (1 : Op ι')) := by
  unfold heteroKron
  simp only [Matrix.kronecker]
  refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
  · rw [Matrix.IsHermitian, Matrix.conjTranspose_kronecker, hO.conjTranspose_eq,
      Matrix.conjTranspose_one]
  · rw [← Matrix.mul_kronecker_mul, hO.mul_self_eq_one, Matrix.one_mul,
      Matrix.one_kronecker_one]

/-- The ampliation `1 ⊗ O` of a binary observable by the identity of the first
tensor factor is a binary observable; this is the mirror of
`isBinaryObservable_heteroKron_one` for the second player's factor in
blueprint `thm:ms-rigidity`. -/
theorem isBinaryObservable_one_heteroKron {ι ι' : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    [Fintype ι'] [DecidableEq ι'] {O : Op ι'} (hO : IsBinaryObservable O) :
    IsBinaryObservable (heteroKron (1 : Op ι) O) := by
  unfold heteroKron
  simp only [Matrix.kronecker]
  refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
  · rw [Matrix.IsHermitian, Matrix.conjTranspose_kronecker, hO.conjTranspose_eq,

  · rw [← Matrix.mul_kronecker_mul, hO.mul_self_eq_one, Matrix.one_mul,

/-- The rank-one density operator associated with an ancillary vector.  This
is the state `|anc⟩⟨anc|` of the extension `ρ' = ρ ⊗ |anc⟩⟨anc|` in
blueprint
`thm:linearity`. -/
noncomputable def ancProj {ι : Type} [Fintype ι]
    (v : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : Op ι :=
  let w := (EuclideanSpace.equiv ι ℂ) v

quantity `d_ρ(S,T)^2` in blueprint

distance of `references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:873-875`. -/
noncomputable def stateDepDistSq {ι : Type} [Fintype ι]
    (S T ρ : Op ι) : ℝ :=
  (Matrix.trace ((S - T)ᴴ * (S - T) * ρ)).re

/-- Each Fourier square `B^u = (hat O^u)^2` of a Hermitian operator family is
positive semidefinite, being the product of a Hermitian matrix with its
adjoint.  This is the positivity half of the assertion that the `B^u` form a
POVM at `references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1098-1099`. -/
theorem operatorFourier_mul_self_posSemidef {t : ℕ}
    {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, (O a).IsHermitian)
    (u : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
    (operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u).PosSemidef := by
  have h := operatorFourier_isHermitian O hO u
  simpa [h.eq] using
    Matrix.posSemidef_conjTranspose_mul_self (operatorFourier O u)

identity `sum_operatorFourier_sq_eq_one`.  This is the POVM to which Naimark's
theorem is applied at `references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1097-1100`. -/
def fourierSquareMeasurement {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]

    (fun u => operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u)
    (fun u => (operatorFourier_mul_self_posSemidef O (fun a => (hO a).1) u).nonneg)
    (sum_operatorFourier_sq_eq_one O hO)

    (u : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
    (fourierSquareMeasurement O hO).effect u =

This file carries out the Fourier-analytic part of the proof of the quantum
linearity theorem of Natarajan and Vidick.  Given binary observables `O^u`
indexed by the Boolean cube `𝔽_2^t` and a positive semidefinite trace-one
operator `ρ`, it expresses the state-dependent multiplicative defect of the
family through the two-query correlation of the linearity test, identifies the
sum of the cubic Fourier coefficients with that correlation, and records the
overlap certificate for the Fourier-square POVM `B^u = (hat O^u)^2` used in the
Naimark-dilation argument.  Pairwise commutation of the observables is never
assumed, and every complex trace is handled through its real part.

## Main results

* `multiplicativeDefect`: the state-dependent squared defect of `O^u O^v`
  from `O^{u+v}`.
* `avg_multiplicativeDefect_eq_two_sub_two_mul_correlation` and
  `avg_multiplicativeDefect_le_two_mul_error`: the average defect equals
  `2 - 2 * (correlation)`, hence is at most `2 * δ` under the correlation
  hypothesis of `exists_exactly_linear_observables`.
* `operatorFourier_cube_trace_eq_correlation`: the identity
  `∑_u Tr_ρ((hat O^u)^3) = E_{a,b} Tr_ρ(O^a O^b O^{a+b})`.
* `fourierSquareMeasurement` and `one_sub_error_le_avg_overlap_fourierSquare`:
  the Fourier-square POVM together with its overlap certificate.

## References

Natarajan--Vidick, arXiv:1610.03574, Theorem 10 with displays (7)--(8) and
its proof, `references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1074-1113`; the state-dependent
distance is defined at lines 866--900 of the same file.  The QPBT paper quotes
the theorem at
`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:711-725` and
invokes it at lines 787--832.  The blueprint statement is blueprint
`thm:linearity`.  The normalization of
the error constant is analyzed in
`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_linearity-distance-normalization.tex`: the exact defect
bound is `2 * δ` for the squared state-dependent operator distance
`stateDepDistSq`, equivalently `δ` for the squared binary-observable distance.
-/
